reasons.rubric: Two-issuer match with a hypothetical telecom issuer and low frequency and stakes, so it needs design and is arguably weak.
reasons.validity: Alumni pricing exists, but a single alumni credential suffices; the telecom binding is unnecessary and no such issuer exists.
reasons.coherence: The stated predicate (same person across two credentials) does not match the verifier's real need (is an alumnus), so the parts fit loosely.
reasons.novelty: Alumni status is close to the degree-proof and student-discount cases but adds a new matching predicate.
reasons.retention_law: A small vendor has no apparent duty to retain the ID or diploma, so this holds.
reasons.linkability: A cross-credential match with no shared identifier is hard, and repeated renewals could be linked unless designed carefully; unclear.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Telecoms have no verifiable-credential product or incentive to issue one for an alumni discount, so this likely fails.
reasons.no_wallet: The vendor would need a wallet-based verifier for a tiny discount, and a staff glance at the card is cheaper, so it fails.

reasons.rubric: A utility-roll membership proof is a simple predicate, but the issuer ecosystem is fragmented and the agency legally needs income and asset data, so it is a weak partial fit.
reasons.validity: Rent subsidy is decided on income, assets and household registration, so a utility-subsidy roll is not sufficient for the decision.
reasons.coherence: The moment mixes an agency verifier, a landlord worry and a different locality, and a hidden address conflicts with the agency needing an occupied dwelling.
reasons.novelty: It overlaps the known utility-subsidy and low-income-subsidy cases, though the housing agency verifier is new.
reasons.retention_law: A government agency processing a subsidy application will likely have to keep lease and application records, so ZK removes little.
reasons.linkability: A roll-membership proof for a single application is not obviously linkable, and no cross-context tracking issue is evident.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Taipower and the Water Corporation are state-linked but have no credential product and little reason to sign roll membership for this.
reasons.no_wallet: Applicants can already submit the documents the agency accepts, and the agency would need to build verifier support, so adoption is doubtful.

reasons.rubric: A threshold on two numbers is simple, but the issuer is not a trusted signer (zkTLS over a page) and frequency is low, so it needs design and a fit of about 3.
reasons.validity: Fleet deposit waivers are plausible and the two thresholds mostly capture reliability, but the platform's terms may forbid automated access and a screenshot-forgery fix is real.
reasons.coherence: The moment, predicate, and zkTLS issuer fit together well and the weaknesses are admitted.
reasons.novelty: Gig-driver reputation for leasing is a moment no known case touches.
reasons.provenance: The data-minimisation borrowing is generic and the screenshot-forgery point is real and shapes the choice of zkTLS, but both are partly decorative; the idea would read nearly the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: A leasing company has no evident legal duty to retain full screenshots, so this holds.
reasons.linkability: zkTLS proofs of aggregate numbers carry no persistent identifier, so this holds.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The platform does not issue anything and may actively oppose scraping of its API, but zkTLS does not need its consent, so it is not blocked outright and is uncertain.
reasons.no_wallet: The driver needs a zkTLS tool and the lessor must run a verifier, which no Taiwanese lessor has today, so adoption is a real hurdle.

reasons.rubric: Poll-scoped uniqueness is a simple predicate, but the telco issuer does not prove residency or ownership, and the issuer ecosystem is fragmented, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: Condominium voting is real, but one unique subscriber is not sufficient since eligibility needs ownership or residency, and the law may require named written ballots and proxies.
reasons.coherence: Ballot secrecy and a telco uniqueness proof pull in different directions because a phone number does not tie to a unit, and the idea concedes this.
reasons.novelty: Community voting is a moment nobody on the known list touches, though the uniqueness predicate resembles the one-person-one-account case.
reasons.provenance: The jury-anonymity and privileged-communication borrowings only motivate wanting privacy and would read the same without them, so they are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: Condominium rules may require named voter records and proxy documents, which is uncertain in Taiwanese law, so I cannot confirm either way.
reasons.linkability: A poll-scoped nullifier does not link across polls, but the single-use scope is designed in and this holds.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: A telco has no reason to issue a one-real-subscriber credential for a building poll, and one person can hold several numbers.
reasons.no_wallet: Residents of a typical building would need a wallet and the committee a verifier, when a simple chat poll or paper ballot is the norm.

reasons.rubric: Student status plus identity match is a modest predicate with two issuers, medium frequency and low stakes, so it is possible but needs design.
reasons.validity: Student concession fares are real, but a clerk also needs the person present and a card glance is the accepted practice, so the match proof adds little.
reasons.coherence: The title says alumni and the body describes current students, and the unlinkability borrowing is not used in the described design.
reasons.novelty: It largely rewords the known degree and scholarship enrolment cases and the sibling alumni idea.
reasons.provenance: The minimal-recording borrowing is already the premise and the blind-token unlinkability is never built into the predicate, so both are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: A transport operator has no evident duty to keep a full ID copy, though some sales records may be kept, so this holds.
reasons.linkability: A match proof at each purchase could link repeated purchases unless unlinkable tokens are used, which the idea mentions but does not design.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Universities may sign enrolment but the wallet credential is a government product, and operators' own student ID systems already exist, so willingness is unclear.
reasons.no_wallet: Counters and kiosks have no wallet verifier and the benefit is small, so adoption fails in practice.

reasons.rubric: Non-membership is a clean yes/no with a government issuer, but the verifier has little duty to check, frequency is moderate, and a fresh proof is needed, so it is a possible fit.
reasons.validity: Border control already checks the register at departure, so an airline check is not a real decision point and a restricted traveler could not even produce the proof.
reasons.coherence: The claim that the verifier learns only one bit conflicts with the fact that failure to produce a proof itself discloses restriction.
reasons.novelty: Exit-restriction checks at departure are a moment nobody on the known list touches.
reasons.provenance: The copyable-ID point and the differential-privacy bound are not used anywhere in the design, so they are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: Airlines are often required to keep passenger travel document data, so ZK may not remove the copy, though I am unsure about Taiwanese law.
reasons.linkability: A signed short-window proof could act as an identifier unless designed to be unlinkable, and the issuer would see each check.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The Immigration Agency would have to expose restriction data tied to court and tax records, which agencies are very unlikely to do for private carriers.
reasons.no_wallet: Airline counters would need a verifier, and passport scanning is mandatory anyway, so the proof can't replace the existing flow.

reasons.rubric: A minimum-balance-over-period predicate is a range-style, multi-day check from a bank issuer, and the foreign verifier is outside the ecosystem, so it needs design.
reasons.validity: Proof of funds is a real step in study abroad, and a bank-signed threshold is sufficient in principle, but foreign offices set their own formats and agents want paper.
reasons.coherence: Predicate, issuer and verifier fit, with the cross-border acceptance problem honestly stated.
reasons.novelty: It is a new moment and predicate distinct from the income-threshold loan case, though bank balance proofs are a familiar shape.
reasons.provenance: Both borrowings only restate that full ID or document copies are over-collection, which any such idea says, so they are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: Foreign universities and embassies may retain submitted financial evidence, but no Taiwanese retention duty is evident, so this is unclear.
reasons.linkability: An aggregate balance proof carries no persistent identifier if the bank signs it appropriately, so this holds.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Taiwanese banks already issue balance certificates and might sign a threshold, though a credential product is uncertain.
reasons.no_wallet: Foreign verifiers have no means to check a Taiwan wallet proof, so the receiving side is missing.

reasons.rubric: A reputation threshold over a zkTLS proof is simple, but the issuer is an unwilling platform, the data is already public, and the moment is occasional, so it is a weak fit.
reasons.validity: Trust matters in high-value private sales, but feedback is public already and a rented or bought account defeats the proof, so the predicate is not sufficient.
reasons.coherence: The moment mixes buyer and seller sides and two verifiers, and the pseudonymity benefit conflicts with the platform account being the identity.
reasons.novelty: Marketplace seller verification is a known case, though this buyer-side and reputation-threshold angle is a new predicate.
reasons.provenance: The unlinkability and selective-disclosure borrowings are generic labels and the idea reads the same without them, so they are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: A private counterparty has no legal duty to retain anything, so this holds.
reasons.linkability: Proof of the same account could be linked across sales if the same account is reused, and the account name is hidden only if unlinked, which is unclear.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The platform issues nothing and may block this, but zkTLS needs no consent, so the outcome is unclear.
reasons.no_wallet: Private individuals and convenience-store services would both need zkTLS tooling, which almost no one has, so adoption fails.
